claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and living with you, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he at school, college, university, or undertaking an apprenticeship or other approved training programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and isn't studying or doing any courses right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 17 and no longer in approved education or training, I need to ask:

**Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that. He just left school and hasn't signed up with careers services or the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask about his current situation:

**Is Alex currently in paid work, and if so, how many hours per week is he working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's not in any paid employment right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name. He doesn't get anything like Universal Credit or ESA himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have one final question:

**Are you living in the UK, and is Alex your biological child, adopted child, or are you his guardian/looking after him in some other arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK, and Alex is my son - he's my biological child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, I need to let you know that **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time**.

Here's why: Child Benefit can be claimed for children under 16, or for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training. Since Alex is 17 and is no longer in approved education or training, and he hasn't registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, he falls outside the eligibility criteria.

However, there is a potential option: if Alex were to register with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services within a certain timeframe of leaving education, you could potentially claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from that registration. If Alex does register in the future, it would be worth contacting HMRC to see if this applies to your situation.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this, or do you have any other children you'd like me to assess?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for explaining that to me. No, Alex is my only child, so I understand I'm not eligible at the moment. I appreciate you taking the time to go through everything with me.
